source_ref.production_note: Vertical 1080x1920 social shortform, series episode 10. Three-part structure: live-action presenter intro (employee carrying a parcel through a bright open-plan office) -> a single continuous handheld real-device in-app demo screen-captured by filming an iPhone in hand -> live-action presenter outro (unboxing). Numbered step badges (1-5) plus a torn-paper caption strip drive a step-by-step tutorial. Scene detector reported 8 segments but several are in-app screen transitions inside one continuous take (status-bar clock runs 10:46 -> 10:48 unbroken, same hand and background); true camera cuts are only intro->demo and demo->outro.

narrative_arc: An employee-host opens with a hook caption promising a way to check a scam account, then walks us through a real-device demo: a secondhand-sneaker seller sends a bank account; the host copies it, opens the banking app, taps transfer, pastes the account, and the app flags it with a red warning ('suspected scam account, reported'); even after entering an amount and tapping send, a warning sheet blocks the transfer; the host closes by replying 'it's a scam' to the seller and signs off promising more hidden tips while unboxing a (legitimately bought) jacket.
creative_device: employee-host step-by-step real-device app demo with numbered torn-paper captions synced to voiceover, building to a red scam-warning payoff

production_signature.signature_note: Two distinct camera modes. Live-action bookends are filmed with a smooth handheld follow/locked-medium on the host in a bright office. The long middle demo is a screen-capture-by-filming approach: a real iPhone held in one hand is shot by a second handheld camera, so the phone drifts with gentle natural handheld motion and the on-screen UI is the real app. No wiggle_3d / lenticular parallax. metrics wiggle hint (mean_abs_shift_x 0.15, sign_flips 0.30) is ordinary handheld jitter, not a deliberate 3D wiggle.

global_layout.layout_note: Whole piece is center-weighted vertical. Captions live in a dedicated lower zone: top headline brush-boxes only in the intro/outro, and a torn-paper caption strip pinned to the lower third throughout the demo, often paired with a blue numbered step badge to its upper-left. The phone (demo) or the host (bookends) occupies the central two-thirds; UI / face never competes with the caption zone.

inferred_creative_thinking.insight: Young users buy and sell a lot secondhand and quietly fear getting scammed on a bank transfer; they don't know their banking app can already check whether the recipient account has been reported as fraudulent.
inferred_creative_thinking.persona: A trustworthy in-house product owner / employee-creator who casually shows real hidden features of the app, peer-to-peer rather than ad-like.
inferred_creative_thinking.moment: The exact moment of a risky secondhand transfer — you've copied a stranger's account and are about to send money.
inferred_creative_thinking.product_role: The app is the quiet safety net: it cross-checks the account against fraud-report data and throws a red warning (and blocks the send) before you lose money.
inferred_creative_thinking.punchline: Even if you ignore the flag and hit send, it stops you — and you can reply '사기네요' to the scammer.
inferred_creative_thinking.differentiator: A real-device, real-UI, step-numbered demo of an actual lesser-known safety feature, narrated by a real employee, ending on a satisfying scam call-out.
inferred_creative_thinking.brand_fit_one_liner: Positions the brand as the bank that actively protects you from fraud, not just one that moves money.

inferred_brief: Make a friendly, credible short-form tutorial (in the ongoing 'Toss hidden services' employee series) that teaches users how to check whether a recipient bank account is a reported scam account before sending money, to drive trust and feature awareness.
